mechanism: Warfarin and aspirin both impair hemostasis (coagulation + platelet inhibition), significantly increasing bleeding risk, especially GI hemorrhage.
action: Monitor INR and signs of bleeding; discuss with prescriber before combining.

mechanism: NSAIDs add an antiplatelet effect and can irritate the gastric mucosa, compounding warfarin-induced bleeding risk.
action: Avoid combination where possible; monitor INR and GI bleeding signs.

mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP2C9/CYP3A4 metabolism of warfarin, raising INR and bleeding risk.
action: Monitor INR closely during and after the antibiotic course; consider an alternative antibiotic.

mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9, decreasing warfarin metabolism and increasing INR.
action: Reduce warfarin dose under prescriber guidance and monitor INR frequently.

mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, blocking simvastatin clearance and raising the risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.
action: Avoid coadministration; hold simvastatin for the duration of the clarithromycin course.

mechanism: Gemfibrozil inhibits simvastatin glucuronidation, greatly increasing myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk.
action: Avoid combination; use an alternative fibrate or statin.

mechanism: Amiodarone reduces digoxin clearance and displaces digoxin from tissue binding, raising serum digoxin levels and toxicity risk.
action: Reduce digoxin dose and monitor serum digoxin levels.

mechanism: Verapamil inhibits P-glycoprotein-mediated digoxin elimination, raising digoxin levels and toxicity risk.
action: Monitor digoxin levels; reduce dose if combined.

mechanism: Both are antifolates; coadministration increases the risk of severe bone-marrow suppression and pancytopenia.
action: Avoid combination; use an alternative antibiotic.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance, raising lithium levels into the toxic range.
action: Monitor lithium levels; prefer alternative analgesia.

mechanism: ACE inhibitor plus potassium-sparing diuretic raises serum potassium, risking hyperkalemia and arrhythmia.
action: Monitor potassium and renal function; avoid in renal impairment.

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, slowing theophylline clearance and causing toxicity (nausea, seizures, arrhythmia).
action: Monitor theophylline levels; reduce dose.

mechanism: Both agents raise serotonin; combined use increases serotonin syndrome risk and lowers the seizure threshold.
action: Monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms; consider an alternative analgesic.

mechanism: SSRI + MAOI can precipitate serotonin syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, agitation) — a life-threatening emergency.
action: Never combine; allow an adequate washout period between agents.

mechanism: PDE5 inhibitors potentiate nitrate vasodilation, causing severe, potentially fatal hypotension.
action: Contraindicated together; do not administer within 24-48 hours of nitrate use.

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing clopidogrel activation and antiplatelet efficacy.
action: Prefer pantoprazole/rabeprazole or consider an alternative.

mechanism: Carbamazepine induces valproate metabolism and both compete for protein binding, altering levels and increasing toxicity.
action: Monitor drug levels and clinical response.

mechanism: Calcium binds levothyroxine in the gut, reducing absorption and impairing thyroid control.
action: Separate doses by at least 4 hours.

mechanism: Both agents prolong the QT interval; coadministration increases the risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes.
action: Monitor ECG; avoid if other QT-prolonging drugs are present.
